title: docs: document supported topologies, extension points, and anti-patterns (alpha)
author: Bruno Silva
commits: docs(readme): add supported topologies section w/ alpha support boundaries
docs(readme): document extension points + examples for endpoints/route hooks
docs(readme): add anti-patterns + common failure modes (DNS/endpoints/NAT)
chore(docs): align terminology with installer + reference architecture
fix(docs): clarify private DNS implications for ECR/STS endpoints
body:
## Summary
This PR adds docs-first clarity on what we support in the VPC Terraform modules (alpha), where we expect customers to extend, and what configurations we explicitly do *not* support.

The goal is to reduce back-and-forth during Private discovery / pilots by making it obvious:
- which subnet/routing/NAT patterns are “Redwood-validated”
- which knobs are safe to turn
- which patterns routinely cause installer failures or day-2 pain (endpoints/DNS, egress, overlapping CIDRs)

This is intentionally README-heavy and intended to be the canonical reference for Solutions Engineering to point customers to during pilot setup.

## What changed
- Root README now includes:
  - Supported topologies (alpha): new VPC vs existing VPC, 2–3 AZ private subnet layout, NAT strategies, and endpoint expectations
  - “Support boundaries” language: what’s supported self-serve vs what is possible but requires PS/SE engagement
  - Extension points: where to attach TGW/VPN/DX, add endpoints, override CIDRs, add SG rules safely
  - Anti-patterns: configurations we repeatedly see cause issues (private DNS off, public egress from private subnets, default VPC usage, AZ name hardcoding)
- Module READMEs updated to link back to the top-level guidance and to standardize terms:
  - “private subnets” = workload/node subnets
  - “public subnets” = ingress/NAT/LB only (not node placement)
  - “endpoint private DNS” requirements and when you can disable it
- Example README updated to include a short “pick your topology” table and a minimal checklist for pilots

## Supported topologies (alpha)
Documented as supported/validated:
1) **Greenfield VPC (recommended)**
   - 1 VPC
   - 2 or 3 AZs
   - Public subnets: ALB/NLB + NAT only
   - Private subnets: EKS nodes / Redwood workloads
   - NAT strategy: default = 1 NAT per AZ (with an explicit note on cost tradeoffs)

2) **Bring-your-own VPC (supported with constraints)**
   - Existing VPC is acceptable if:
     - non-overlapping RFC1918 CIDR ranges with customer network
     - private subnets have deterministic egress path (NAT, proxy, or no-internet + full endpoints)
     - required endpoints are present (or module is used to create them)

Documented as “possible but not alpha-supported without engagement”:
- Single-AZ production deployments (ok for dev/sandbox)
- Complex hub-and-spoke with TGW route propagation across multiple VPCs (we provide hooks/outputs, but don’t encode full enterprise routing policy)
- On-prem-only egress with proxy chain customization beyond the module’s current SG patterns

## Extension points (documented)
- **Route table hooks**: outputs and examples for adding TGW/VPN/DX routes without forking the module
- **Additional VPC endpoints**: pattern for adding interface endpoints beyond the defaults and keeping DNS behavior consistent
- **Egress tightening**: recommended approach for least-privilege egress using prefix lists, endpoint security groups, and per-destination rules (without “allow all 0.0.0.0/0”)
- **Logging destinations**: flow logs destination patterns called out (CloudWatch vs S3) with “customer-owned bucket” guidance
- **Tagging**: consistent tagging strategy and why changing Name tags is discouraged (module assumes stable identifiers for outputs)

## Anti-patterns / common failure modes
- Disabling private DNS on **ECR API/DKR** endpoints without replacing name resolution (results in image pull failures)
- “Private subnets” with a route to IGW (confusing, makes egress auditing harder, and breaks assumptions for private deployments)
- Overlapping CIDRs with on-prem or other VPCs when planning DX/VPN (leads to brittle routing and hard-to-debug resolver behavior)
- Hardcoding AZ names (e.g., us-east-1a) instead of using `data.aws_availability_zones` ordering
- Treating the module as a general-purpose enterprise VPC framework (this is intentionally opinionated and narrow for Redwood Private)

## Why now
SE feedback from recent Private discovery calls is that customers need a single “what do we need to run Redwood Private in a VPC” doc that also calls out what will break. Until now the information was spread across Slack threads and verbal guidance.

## Screenshots / snippets (illustrative)
Included a short table in README:
- Topology: Greenfield VPC / Existing VPC
- AZs: 2–3 (supported) / 1 (dev only)
- Egress: NAT per AZ (default) / proxy-only (supported with constraints)
- Endpoints: required set documented + installer alignment note

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Link the “Required endpoints” list to the installer preflight checks once that PR lands (tracked in installer repo)
- Add a small diag section in docs/operational-notes.md for DNS resolver config knobs (VPC resolver, node resolv.conf)

---

## Review conversation highlights

**Markus Klein (Solutions Eng):**
“Can we add explicit language on ‘supported during alpha’ vs ‘possible with PS engagement’? Customers read this as a contract.”

**Bruno Silva (author):**
“Added a ‘Support boundaries (alpha)’ section and updated phrasing to ‘validated defaults’ + ‘engagement required’ for hub/spoke and TGW propagation.”

**Victor Alvarez (Networking):**
“The NAT section should be clear that 1-per-AZ is the default and why; also call out that single NAT can become an AZ dependency.”

**Bruno:**
“Updated NAT guidance with a cost vs availability paragraph and recommended defaults; added an explicit note that single NAT is acceptable for dev/test only.”

**Hanae Suzuki (Security):**
“Please avoid suggesting broad egress rules as an extension point; recommend endpoint-based egress and destination-based rules. Also ensure we’re not implying we manage customer SIEM.”

**Bruno:**
“Adjusted ‘Egress tightening’ section to recommend endpoint SG + prefix list approach; removed the ‘temporary allow-all’ wording. Updated logging section to ‘SIEM integration is customer-managed; module only delivers logs to configured destinations’.”

**Irene Choi (Infra):**
“Make sure module docs don’t promise compatibility with every enterprise topology. The whole point is fewer knobs.”

**Bruno:**
“Added a ‘non-goals’ callout in README and tightened wording in the extension points section to emphasize supported hooks/outputs rather than fully-custom routing.”

**Nina Petrova (Private Deployments):**
“Please call out that EKS private endpoint + endpoints/DNS is a common source of confusion; explicitly mention installer expectations.”

**Bruno:**
“Added an ‘Installer alignment’ subsection with: required endpoints, private DNS guidance, and a note that the installer performs preflight validation and will fail fast on missing ECR endpoints.”

---

## CI
All checks green. Ran link check locally to ensure README anchors are stable.

## Merge
- Merged via squash
- No behavior change; docs only
